Category: Cybersecurity
Importance: 8
Search agents are vulnerable to attacks where factual evidence can mislead their results. This phenomenon, termed lazy grounding, can occur when search agents adopt answers from closely related questions, resulting in a reduction in accuracy and potential misinformation despite the evidence being technically true. Researchers recommend that search agents improve defenses not just against misinformation, but also against the misapplication of factual information.

 - Search agents can be misled by factual evidence related to nearby questions.
 - Lazy grounding can reduce the accuracy of search agents by as much as 17.3 points.
 - Robust search agents must defend against both misinformation and misapplication of factual evidence.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30303

Research on the complexity of the $s$-Club Cluster Edge Deletion problem reveals that it is W[1]-hard parameterized by pathwidth plus the maximum number of $s$-clubs. The study also demonstrates fixed-parameter tractability under certain structural parameters and presents a bicriteria approximation scheme for specific graph types. Furthermore, it initiates investigation into the directed variant of the problem, which similarly exhibits computational hardness.

 - $s$-Club Cluster Edge Deletion problem is W[1]-hard under specific parameterizations.
 - The problem is tractable under certain structural parameters.
 - A new approximation scheme is introduced for particular classes of graphs.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07065

The exposition discusses the historical viewpoints of economists regarding price stability and its implications for economic cycles, particularly during significant downturns such as the Great Depression. It highlights the critique of central banking policies that aim to maintain stable prices, suggesting that these policies may contribute to economic imbalances and eventual recessions.

 - Historical economists like Irving Fisher and John Maynard Keynes promoted price stability as a solution to economic downturns.
 - Criticism of central banking includes the view that monetary policies aimed at preventing falling prices may lead to misallocated resources and economic cycles of boom and bust.
